A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same structured visual-reasoning work, renamed from LLaVA-o1 to LLaVA-CoT. Their text, figures and tables support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v3 additionally contains readable Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning evaluations, training ablations and inference-search experiments in Tables 2–7.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and ablations, revises reported results, and adds supplementary examples of generated responses.

M1.justification: Both versions use four tagged reasoning stages, full-parameter fine-tuning of Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct, and stage-level search with pairwise response selection. Appendices B–D explain the existing data-generation, training and selection procedures; they do not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: The ten training sources, six evaluation benchmarks and three reasoning-focused benchmark subsets are retained. The added illustrative cases concern visual question-answering capabilities already covered, including open-ended responses. The AI2D testing-variant issue concerns protocol within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds Qwen2-VL-7B to the evaluated comparator set. Table 2 also withdraws the AI2D results for the direct-training and tag-removal comparators. Other existing VLM comparators and the best-of-N and sentence-level search comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v3 reports an AI2D protocol error: AI2D_TEST_NO_MASK was used instead of the intended AI2D_TEST, invalidating the marked ablation results in Table 2. This revises the documented testing account without establishing that those ablations were rerun. Other stated splits and search budgets remain unchanged; the appendix hyperparameters and subset criteria are newly disclosed details.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds two cases examining inappropriate refusal and mistaken claims that a question is unclear; Appendix F adds fill-in-the-blank and open-ended response comparisons. Table 2 loses the AI2D component of the training ablations pending correction. The remaining tag, training-data, skill-area and beam-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly discloses training seed 42. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. This is additional seed information, without evidence of increased replication.

E6.justification: AI2D scores are revised from 85.7 to 78.7 without search and from 87.5 to 78.8 with beam size 2; two AI2D ablation scores and their averages are withdrawn. Table 7 averages consequently change from 64.3/65.8 to 63.1/64.3, moving the unscaled model below Gemini-1.5-Pro and GPT-4o-mini. Qwen2-VL-7B results, averaging 65.9, and new qualitative cases are added. These materially revise the reported comparative results; the AI2D protocol issue prevents interpreting them as a same-setting model deterioration. Other five-benchmark scores and MMVet search results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs, and the retained mathematical worked examples are unchanged. The supplementary procedural descriptions and benchmark-category explanations do not introduce new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract reduces the claimed base-model advantage from 8.9% to 7.4%, narrowing the quantitative headline. The central contributions—autonomous structured reasoning, the annotated training dataset and scalable stage-level search—and the claim of outperforming selected larger or closed models remain.

C2.justification: Appendices A and F add specific interpretations connecting failures to question misinterpretation, premature judgments of ambiguity and insufficiently specific answers. The AI2D footnote newly acknowledges invalid ablation evidence and pending corrections. Existing explanations of structured reasoning and the computational limitation on beam-size testing are retained.

D1.justification: Appendices B–E substantially expand reproducibility information: generation and verification prompts, answer-conditioned filtering, stage-specific judging instructions, and exact reasoning-subset categories. Table 8 supplies llama_recipes/FSDP settings, learning rate 1e-5, three epochs, batch size 4 and context length 4096, among other parameters. The abstract newly reports public code, dataset and weights with an access link; v1 only promises dataset release. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated procedural changes.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds sequential instruction tuning by Hu et al., Prism's separation of perception and reasoning, and MSG's forced chain-of-thought approach. Qwen2-VL is also newly cited with its comparison results. These additions acknowledge relevant predecessors while retaining the overall research positioning and tagged-reasoning novelty claim.

P1.justification: The model and dataset are renamed throughout, author/affiliation text is updated, and related-work passages receive localized revisions. v3 adds Appendix A–F headings and supporting cross-references, while preserving the main section order and most existing prose.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1 with revised scores and Figure 4 with clearer candidate-branch connections. It adds case-study Figures 6–7, hyperparameter Table 8 and boxed prompts. Table 7 gains a comparator row and Table 2 gains an error note; the established main-text display organization remains largely intact.

improvement.justification: Appendices B–E address substantial reproducibility omissions in v1 by documenting the data-generation, training, response-selection and benchmark-subset procedures. v3 also makes the AI2D testing error explicit and revises the headline results, improving transparency despite lower reported performance. Corrected AI2D ablations remain unavailable, limiting that comparison, but the substantial gains in reproducibility and accountability outweigh this remaining gap.
